Read the following unseen passage and answer Questions 5, 6 and 7.

In a fictional village called Sonapur, a mobile library began visiting in March 2024. The librarian, Rupa, carries books in a small van. Every Tuesday she parks beside the community centre. Children can borrow two books each for one week. A local youth group repairs damaged covers and helps return books to the shelves. Rupa also reads aloud to younger children, who are not yet ready to read alone. The library brings stories closer to families who live far from a public library.

5. Complete the information table from the passage.
1. Village: __________
2. Start: __________
3. Librarian: __________
4. Visit day: __________
5. Borrowing period: __________

6. Write True or False. Correct each false statement.
a) The library travels in a van.
b) It stops at the railway station.
c) Children may borrow two books each.
d) The books may be kept for a month.
e) A youth group helps repair covers.

7. Write a brief summary of the passage in your own words.
items.explanation:
5. Information transfer:
1. Sonapur
2. March 2024
3. Rupa
4. Tuesday
5. one week

6. True/False:
a) True
b) False: It stops beside the community centre.
c) True
d) False: They may be kept for one week.
e) True

7. Sample summary: A mobile library brings books to Sonapur each Tuesday. Rupa and local volunteers help children borrow and enjoy books.
items.page: Original fictional practice; model-test pattern, not a source transcription.

Read the following unseen passage and answer Questions 5, 6 and 7.

At fictional Shapla School, students began a rainwater collection project in June 2023. Their science teacher, Mr Rahman, helped them place a covered tank beside the school garden. Rainwater from the roof passes through a simple screen before entering the tank. The group uses this water on flower beds, not for drinking. On Thursdays, a team checks the tank and records the water level. They also clear leaves from the screen. The project teaches students how a useful resource can be collected and managed carefully.

5. Complete the information table from the passage.
1. School: __________
2. Start: __________
3. Teacher: __________
4. Tank location: __________
5. Checking day: __________

6. Write True or False. Correct each false statement.
a) The tank collects rainwater.
b) The water is used for drinking.
c) The tank is uncovered.
d) Students check the tank on Thursdays.
e) A screen helps keep leaves out.

7. Write a brief summary of the passage in your own words.
items.explanation:
5. Information transfer:
1. Shapla School
2. June 2023
3. Mr Rahman
4. beside the school garden
5. Thursday

6. True/False:
a) True
b) False: It is used on flower beds, not for drinking.
c) False: The tank is covered.
d) True
e) True

7. Sample summary: Students at Shapla School collect rainwater for their garden and maintain the system with their teacher.

Read the following unseen passage and answer Questions 5, 6 and 7.

In the fictional town of Chandipur, a community repair workshop opened in January 2022. Its organiser, Farid, wanted to reduce waste and help neighbours learn useful skills. The workshop meets on the first Saturday of each month in the town hall. Volunteers show visitors how to mend torn clothes and repair simple wooden objects. People bring their own damaged items, and no fee is charged for instruction. The organisers do not attempt unsafe electrical repairs. They advise visitors to consult qualified professionals for those jobs.

5. Complete the information table from the passage.
1. Town: __________
2. Opening: __________
3. Organiser: __________
4. Meeting place: __________
5. Meeting time: __________

6. Write True or False. Correct each false statement.
a) Visitors pay a fee for instruction.
b) Volunteers help mend clothes.
c) The workshop repairs all electrical devices.
d) Farid organised the workshop.
e) The workshop meets every day.

7. Write a brief summary of the passage in your own words.
items.explanation:
5. Information transfer:
1. Chandipur
2. January 2022
3. Farid
4. town hall
5. the first Saturday of each month

6. True/False:
a) False: Instruction is free.
b) True
c) False: It does not attempt unsafe electrical repairs.
d) True
e) False: It meets on the first Saturday of each month.

7. Sample summary: Farid’s community workshop teaches simple repairs for free and refers unsafe electrical work to qualified professionals.

Read the following unseen passage and answer Questions 5, 6 and 7.

In fictional Madhabpur, neighbours turned an unused plot into a community garden in April 2021. A local gardener named Asha advised them to test the soil and choose suitable plants. The group grew spinach, beans and marigolds in separate beds. Members meet on Friday afternoons to water, weed and share the work. They keep a list of tasks so that no one has to do everything alone. Some of the vegetables are shared among participating families, while the flowers make the area more cheerful.

5. Complete the information table from the passage.
1. Village: __________
2. Start: __________
3. Adviser: __________
4. Meeting time: __________
5. One vegetable grown: __________

6. Write True or False. Correct each false statement.
a) The garden was once an unused plot.
b) Asha advised the group.
c) The group meets on Monday mornings.
d) Only flowers are grown.
e) Some vegetables are shared with participating families.

7. Write a brief summary of the passage in your own words.
items.explanation:
5. Information transfer:
1. Madhabpur
2. April 2021
3. Asha
4. Friday afternoons
5. spinach or beans

6. True/False:
a) True
b) True
c) False: It meets on Friday afternoons.
d) False: Vegetables and flowers are grown.
e) True

7. Sample summary: Neighbours in Madhabpur share tasks and grow vegetables and flowers in a community garden.

Read the following unseen passage and answer Questions 5, 6 and 7.

A fictional environmental club at Padma School organised a riverbank clean-up in September 2024. The club leader, Nila, first asked local officials where the group could work safely. Twenty students joined with teachers and adult volunteers. Wearing gloves, they collected plastic bottles and wrappers along a short stretch of bank. They placed the waste in marked bags for collection by the local authority. The group avoided entering the water or handling sharp objects. Afterwards, they discussed how to reduce waste before it reaches the river.

5. Complete the information table from the passage.
1. School: __________
2. Month: __________
3. Club leader: __________
4. Student participants: __________
5. Protective item: __________

6. Write True or False. Correct each false statement.
a) Twenty students took part.
b) Students collected waste while swimming.
c) Nila consulted local officials about safety.
d) The group handled sharp objects.
e) Waste was placed in marked bags.

7. Write a brief summary of the passage in your own words.
items.explanation:
5. Information transfer:
1. Padma School
2. September 2024
3. Nila
4. twenty
5. gloves

6. True/False:
a) True
b) False: They worked on the bank and avoided entering the water.
c) True
d) False: It avoided handling sharp objects.
e) True

7. Sample summary: A school club worked with adults to clean a riverbank safely and discuss ways to prevent waste.

Read the following unseen passage and answer Questions 5, 6 and 7.

A fictional school in Rangapur planned an inclusive sports day in November 2023. Teacher Salma invited students to suggest activities that people with different abilities could enjoy. The programme included a seated ball game, a walking event and a team puzzle. Volunteers marked a clear route to the field and placed drinking water near the entrance. The event began at nine in the morning. Students could choose whether to compete or assist. At the end, everyone received a thank-you card for taking part.

5. Complete the information table from the passage.
1. Place: __________
2. Date: __________
3. Teacher: __________
4. Start time: __________
5. One activity: __________

6. Write True or False. Correct each false statement.
a) Students could suggest activities.
b) The event began at noon.
c) The route to the field was marked.
d) Only winners received thank-you cards.
e) Students had to compete.

7. Write a brief summary of the passage in your own words.
items.explanation:
5. Information transfer:
1. Rangapur
2. November 2023
3. Salma
4. nine in the morning
5. seated ball game or walking event or team puzzle

6. True/False:
a) True
b) False: It began at nine in the morning.
c) True
d) False: Everyone received a thank-you card.
e) False: They could choose to compete or assist.

7. Sample summary: A school planned an inclusive sports day with varied activities and opportunities to participate or help.

Read the following unseen passage and answer Questions 5, 6 and 7.

In fictional Banshgram, a seed exchange began in August 2022. A farmer named Jahanara arranged the first meeting under a large banyan tree. Families brought clearly labelled packets of vegetable seeds and discussed how they had stored them. A school teacher kept a notebook of the varieties exchanged. The group agreed that anyone accepting seeds should ask local experts about suitable growing conditions. Members met again three months later to discuss which plants had grown well. Their aim was to share experience, not to promise that every seed would grow.

5. Complete the information table from the passage.
1. Village: __________
2. Beginning: __________
3. Organiser: __________
4. Meeting place: __________
5. Second meeting: __________

6. Write True or False. Correct each false statement.
a) The packets were labelled.
b) The first meeting took place in a cinema.
c) The group promised every seed would grow.
d) A teacher recorded the varieties.
e) The second meeting occurred three months later.

7. Write a brief summary of the passage in your own words.
items.explanation:
5. Information transfer:
1. Banshgram
2. August 2022
3. Jahanara
4. under a banyan tree
5. three months later

6. True/False:
a) True
b) False: It took place under a banyan tree.
c) False: It made no such promise.
d) True
e) True

7. Sample summary: A village seed exchange enabled families to share seeds and growing experiences while seeking local advice.

Read the following unseen passage and answer Questions 5, 6 and 7.

At fictional Shaluk School, a class began keeping a weather diary in July 2024. Each morning, two students looked at the sky and recorded whether it was sunny, cloudy or rainy. Their teacher, Kamal, showed them how to read a thermometer kept in a shaded place. They wrote the temperature at eight o’clock and compared their notes at the end of each week. The diary did not predict storms; for warnings, the class listened to official weather reports. The activity helped students practise careful observation.

5. Complete the information table from the passage.
1. School: __________
2. Start: __________
3. Teacher: __________
4. Temperature time: __________
5. Thermometer location: __________

6. Write True or False. Correct each false statement.
a) The class recorded the weather each morning.
b) The thermometer was kept in direct sunlight.
c) Kamal taught the students to read the thermometer.
d) The diary itself predicted storms.
e) The students compared notes weekly.

7. Write a brief summary of the passage in your own words.
items.explanation:
5. Information transfer:
1. Shaluk School
2. July 2024
3. Kamal
4. eight o’clock
5. a shaded place

6. True/False:
a) True
b) False: It was kept in a shaded place.
c) True
d) False: The class relied on official weather reports for warnings.
e) True

7. Sample summary: Students kept a weather diary to practise observation and used official reports for storm warnings.

Read the following unseen passage and answer Questions 5, 6 and 7.

In fictional Jamalpur School, older and younger students started a reading partnership in February 2023. Every Wednesday, pairs meet in the library for twenty minutes. Older students listen while younger partners read an age-appropriate story aloud. The organiser, teacher Rina, reminds partners to be patient and offer help only when needed. Students may also discuss the pictures or choose another book. The programme does not replace regular lessons; it gives children another opportunity to practise and enjoy reading.

5. Complete the information table from the passage.
1. School: __________
2. Start: __________
3. Meeting day: __________
4. Session length: __________
5. Organiser: __________

6. Write True or False. Correct each false statement.
a) The partners meet in the library.
b) Each meeting lasts two hours.
c) Older students listen to younger readers.
d) The programme replaces all regular lessons.
e) Rina asks partners to be patient.

7. Write a brief summary of the passage in your own words.
items.explanation:
5. Information transfer:
1. Jamalpur School
2. February 2023
3. Wednesday
4. twenty minutes
5. teacher Rina

6. True/False:
a) True
b) False: It lasts twenty minutes.
c) True
d) False: It gives additional practice and does not replace lessons.
e) True

7. Sample summary: A school reading partnership pairs older and younger students for patient, enjoyable library practice.

Read the following unseen passage and answer Questions 5, 6 and 7.

In fictional Rupnagar, a community centre installed a handwashing station in May 2024. The centre manager, Tania, placed it near the main entrance. A local volunteer checks the soap and water every morning. Children helped make a poster showing when to wash hands, including before eating and after using the toilet. The centre also keeps the path to the station clear for visitors using mobility aids. The project is simple, but regular maintenance is necessary to keep the station useful.

5. Complete the information table from the passage.
1. Place: __________
2. Installation: __________
3. Manager: __________
4. Location: __________
5. Supply check: __________

6. Write True or False. Correct each false statement.
a) The station is near the entrance.
b) The supplies are checked once a year.
c) Children helped make a poster.
d) The path is kept clear.
e) The station needs no maintenance.

7. Write a brief summary of the passage in your own words.
items.explanation:
5. Information transfer:
1. Rupnagar
2. May 2024
3. Tania
4. near the main entrance
5. every morning

6. True/False:
a) True
b) False: A volunteer checks them every morning.
c) True
d) True
e) False: It needs regular maintenance.

7. Sample summary: A community centre maintains an accessible handwashing station and teaches visitors when to wash their hands.

In the fictional town of Nabinagar, Arif learned basic bicycle maintenance from his aunt. In December 2023, they held a free demonstration at a youth centre. They showed twelve students how to check tyre pressure and clean a bicycle chain. They also explained why brakes should be inspected before a ride. The students wore gloves while working and used tools under adult supervision. Arif reminded them that a damaged brake should be repaired by a qualified mechanic before the bicycle is used.

5. Complete the information table from the passage.
1. Town: __________
2. Demonstration date: __________
3. Young organiser: __________
4. Venue: __________
5. Students attending: __________

6. Write True or False. Correct each false statement.
a) Arif learned from his aunt.
b) The demonstration was held at a youth centre.
c) Twelve teachers attended as students.
d) The students worked without supervision.
e) A damaged brake should be ignored.

7. Write a brief summary of the passage in your own words.
items.explanation:
5. Information transfer:
1. Nabinagar
2. December 2023
3. Arif
4. youth centre
5. twelve

6. True/False:
a) True
b) True
c) False: Twelve students attended.
d) False: They worked under adult supervision.
e) False: It should be repaired by a qualified mechanic before riding.

7. Sample summary: Arif and his aunt taught students simple bicycle checks and emphasised safe, supervised repairs.

Read the following unseen passage and answer Questions 5, 6 and 7.

In fictional Dighalia School, students created a shared noticeboard in January 2024. Their teacher, Bina, placed it outside the library so that pupils could easily find it. Each Monday, a student team updates the board with club meetings and school events. Before posting, the team checks dates with a teacher. The board also has a space for suggestions, but private personal information is not displayed. At the end of the month, old notices are removed and paper that can be reused is saved.

1. School: __________
2. Created: __________
3. Teacher: __________
4. Location: __________
5. Update day: __________

6. Write True or False. Correct each false statement.
a) The noticeboard is outside the library.
b) A student team updates it every Monday.
c) Personal private information is displayed.
d) Dates are checked with a teacher.
e) Old notices are never removed.

7. Write a brief summary of the passage in your own words.
items.explanation:
5. Information transfer:
1. Dighalia School
2. January 2024
3. Bina
4. outside the library
5. Monday

6. True/False:
a) True
b) True
c) False: Private personal information is not displayed.
d) True
e) False: They are removed at the end of the month.

7. Sample summary: A school noticeboard shares checked event information while protecting privacy and reusing paper.
